'''Stacking''' is the practice of holding several credentials that cross fields, rather than one that goes deep in a single one. It is the central strategic idea of the [[Making Money Certificate Pathways|certificate pathways]] hub, and it is where short certificates stop being small.

== Why one certificate is weak and three are strong ==

A single credential places you in a queue with everyone else holding it, and the queue is sorted by experience — which a newcomer does not have. Three credentials that cross fields place you in a much shorter queue, often a queue of one, because the combination is rarer than any of its parts.

The combination also changes ''what'' you are. A childcare credential is a qualification to be employed. A childcare credential plus food-safety certification plus paediatric first aid is a qualification to be '''contracted''' — to go into homes as a nanny, a tutor or a private carer, to run provision in a church hall, or to be the named qualified person on someone else's operation.

The rule that follows: '''plan the second certificate while taking the first.''' The budget for certificate one should contain the course fee for certificate two.

== The bilateral career path ==

The strongest version of stacking is to add a '''second discipline that applies to every field''', so that your original expertise and the new one multiply rather than add.

The clearest example is '''project management'''. Project-management credentials are not tied to an industry; they attach to whatever the holder already knows. The result is a role that exists in every sector — an IT project manager, a construction project manager, a pyrotechnics project manager, an events project manager — in which the industry knowledge is yours and the method is transferable. That is a ''bilateral'' path: two tracks that reinforce each other, rather than one track with a ceiling.

Other disciplines behave the same way:
* '''Coaching and instruction''' — applies to any field in which someone must be brought up to competence. See [[Personal Training and Coaching Certifications]].
* '''Teaching and training design''' — turns practitioner knowledge into a product; a practitioner who can train is who organisations send.
* '''Records, payroll and administration''' — the back office exists in every organisation. See [[Payroll Certifications FPC and CPP]].
* '''Language''' — see [[Teaching English Abroad TEFL and TESOL]] and the [[CEFR The Common European Framework of Reference for Languages|CEFR scale]].

== Crossing out of a field ==

Stacking is also the mechanism for '''leaving''' a field without starting over. Someone whose entire record is in childcare is not confined to children: adding a fitness or coaching certification converts the demonstrable skills — supervision, safety, instruction, patience under pressure, documentation — into a credential that serves adults. The experience is not discarded; it is relabelled into a market that recognises it.

That is the general principle. Experience is rarely the obstacle. The credential that lets an employer ''read'' the experience is the obstacle, and it is usually cheap.

== Building for the record ==

Two further points worth holding:

'''Prefer institutions whose names carry.''' Where a recognised university or a known body offers coursework at low or no cost, take that one over an equivalent from an unknown issuer. The content may be identical; the line on the file is not.

'''Check who accredits before paying.''' The difference between a credential that survives scrutiny and one that does not is the body behind it. See [[Accreditation Bodies IACET ANSI and CHEA]].

Programmes across fourteen industries are indexed at [https://credentials.soapbox.community credentials.soapbox.community].
